name: DeadLetterRoute
purpose: Named destination where undeliverable or repeatedly failed messages are routed after the redelivery budget is exhausted so they can be inspected or replayed.
invariants: A message delivered more than max_deliveries times MUST be routed to destination_topic and NEVER returned to the main topic.
The original EventEnvelope id and source ALWAYS survive routing so downstream audit can correlate.
max_deliveries MUST be a positive integer; zero or negative values SHALL raise a configuration error.
Routing to the dead letter destination CANNOT itself dead letter recursively in the same route.
The sink MUST record the terminal failure reason so operators can decide whether to replay.
extension_contract: Backends register a DeadLetterSink adapter per transport (Dapr deadLetterTopic, Kafka DLT, NATS dedicated stream) and the runtime composes it with the TopicBus; custom policies extend via a decorator that chooses different destinations based on failure type.
consumption_example:
async def park(sink, envelope: EventEnvelope, err: str) -> None:
    route = DeadLetterRoute(source_topic='orders', destination_topic='orders.dlq', max_deliveries=5)
    await sink.send(route, envelope, err, attempt=route.max_deliveries + 1)

sources.source: Dapr 1.14 Publish and Subscribe building block overview

sources.locator: kafka.apache.org/documentation/ intro_concepts_and_terms discussion of retry topics and DLT pattern

why_essential: Without a shared dead letter contract every consumer invents its own failure bucket and loses replay ability; standardizing the route lets audit, replay and alerting reuse one surface.
alternatives_considered: Logging failed messages to stdout only which is not replayable
Parking lot queues coded per tool which diverge in schema and ownership
